belongs_to: 3.1 Q4 (book p.56): "There are 5 children in a group, all of different heights. Can they stand such that four of them say 1 and the last one says 0? Why or why not?"
description: Line-up of 5 stick figures, left to right, getting steadily taller (strictly increasing heights; head-centre-to-foot on the page picture in px: 33, 51, 60, 72, 88; figure 5 is the tallest, figure 1 the shortest). Stick-figure drawing: each child = solid black filled circle head (about 18 px across on the page picture), a thin black body line with two arm strokes forming a V under the head, and two leg strokes; all children stand on one common ground line. Above each head a white speech bubble (thin black oval outline with a small pointed tail pointing down at the head) holds one bold black digit. Black on white, no colour, no other text. Bubble digits left to right: 1, 1, 1, 1, 0. Rule check (each child says the number of taller neighbours): figures 1-4 each have exactly one taller neighbour (the child on their right) so say 1; figure 5 (tallest, at the right end) has none so says 0. Printed under the answer sentence 'Yes, they can, if they are standing in ascending order of height.'
